match.reason: The closest bank point, eco-tax-reform, covers tax reform in general with three goals (simplicity, fairness and growth), so it is broader than the new point's focus on supply-side tax changes that reward work, saving and investment or cut business costs, and it does not link tax reform to aggregate supply.

draft.title: Tax reform
card: Tax reform is a change to the tax system. As a budgetary supply-side policy, its aim is to lift the economy's productive capacity, or aggregate supply, over the longer term.
Work
lower income tax rates or a higher tax-free threshold can raise the reward for working. This may encourage more people to join the workforce or to work more hours.
Saving and investment
tax breaks on business investment or on returns from saving can encourage firms to buy more capital, such as machinery. More capital can lift productivity.
Cost of business
simpler tax rules or lower company tax can cut the cost of doing business. Lower costs can let firms produce more at each price level.
draft.remember: Tax reform aims to lift supply by rewarding work, saving and investment, or by cutting business costs.

a.q: Why might a lower company tax rate help lift aggregate supply?
opts: It cuts firms' costs and may encourage more investment
It cuts household spending and so lowers inflation
It raises government spending on schools and training
It raises demand by lifting the price of imports
a.why: A lower company tax rate can cut the cost of doing business and leave firms with more funds to invest in capital. Both can lift productive capacity. It is not mainly a way of cutting household spending, which would be a demand-side effect.
a.clue: Think about what firms gain when they pay less tax.

b.q: The government raises the tax-free threshold, so workers keep more of each extra dollar they earn. Which supply-side effect is it aiming for?
opts: More people may take jobs or work more hours
Firms may buy more machinery to raise productivity
Workers may gain skills through vocational training
Firms may face lower costs from better roads and ports
b.why: A higher tax-free threshold raises the reward for working, so it may encourage more labour to be supplied. The effect on machinery comes from investment tax breaks. Skills and roads belong to other policies, not to tax reform.
b.clue: Look at what the change does to take-home pay for work.

a.best: It cuts firms' costs and may encourage more investment

b.best: More people may take jobs or work more hours

problems.detail: The stem says raising the tax-free threshold lets workers 'keep more of each extra dollar they earn'. That is only true for income in the newly untaxed band. Workers already earning above the threshold keep the same share of each extra dollar; they gain a fixed amount of take-home pay instead. Reword to something like 'so workers keep more of what they earn'.
The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('may'), and it is slightly longer than the others. A student could pick it without knowing the idea.
